Law

Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam

← Back to search
About this programme

UCR currently cannot construct a sufficiently close programme for a meaningful curriculum comparison.

VU Law develops legal reasoning across Dutch private, criminal, constitutional and administrative law, European and international law. Students learn to interpret legal sources, solve cases, argue in writing and speech, and progress to advanced doctrinal study, pleading and independent legal research.

UCR offers substantive study of comparative law, human rights, criminal justice, public international and European law, private law and business law. These courses do not form a complete programme with the sustained Dutch doctrinal progression and integrated legal methods, procedure and research that define this degree. We therefore show the verified VU curriculum without presenting a UCR programme as a comparable alternative.

Academic year: 2026–2027

The 180 EC pathway comprises 150 EC of compulsory legal study and 30 EC of open minor or approved study. PPI 1, PPI 2 and Dutch language testing are integrated credit or grade requirements. Thesis entry requires 120 EC including Legal Skills; pleading requires 99 EC including Legal Skills. Course prerequisites, attendance and open-study approval rules apply.
